title: ILAN: The Interference- and Locality-Aware NUMA Scheduler
problem: OpenMP default scheduler is topology-agnostic; poor data locality and task interference on NUMA systems
motivation: Modern HPC uses NUMA; need interference-aware and locality-preserving task scheduling
method: ILAN is a task scheduler for LLVM OpenMP on NUMA systems—computers where different processors have varying-speed access to different memory regions. It uses moldability (changing how many parallel tasks run based on the situation) to reduce interference, the slowdown when too many tasks fight over the same memory and cache. It also organizes tasks hierarchically—scheduling at different levels from processor sockets down to individual cores—so each task runs near the memory it needs to access.
key_novelty: ILAN reduces task interference and improves data locality on NUMA systems through hierarchical task scheduling that's aware of the hardware's memory topology (how different processors connect to different memory at different speeds).
contributions: Hierarchical scheduling for NUMA data locality
13.2% average, 45.8% max speedup on 64-core AMD Zen 4
